title: ledge event
description: A card in the bar: a headline, what clicking it does, and what else its kind shows. Send it to POST /event, or pipe it to `ledge event`.

time.description: An ISO 8601 time, or a duration from when it's sent such as "30m", "4h" or "2d".

color.description: A named colour (green, yellow, red, blue or gray) or a #rrggbb hex colour.

url.description: Clicking runs `open <url>`, so it opens in whatever app handles it (https: in your browser, vscode: in VS Code). Must start with a scheme.

web.description: An http(s) url, opened in your browser.

inline.description: Text: a string, a span ({"type": "strong", "text": "failed"}), or an array of strings and spans, run together. Shown as text, never as HTML.

span.description: Text styled or linked: strong, em, mono (fixed-width, such as a name in code) or link (http(s) only). A strong, em or link's text can have spans of its own.

cell.description: A table cell or a field's value: a number, text, or a row of buttons ({"type": "buttons", "items": [...]}).

button.description: A button, with a dot in its colour. Clicking it opens its `url`, runs its `command` (only if commands are allowed, as for cards; otherwise it's disabled) or, with "dismiss": true, dismisses the event. With none of them it does nothing.

not.description: only one of `url`, `command` and `dismiss` can be set: clicking a button does one thing

block.description: One part of a report. `type` says which, and so which other properties it takes. All text is shown as plain text, never as HTML.

heading.description: A section heading, level 1 (largest) to 6. Default 2: the report's title is its window's.

paragraph.description: A paragraph. Line breaks in it are kept.

table.description: A table: column headings, and rows of cells. A row with fewer cells than columns leaves the rest empty; extra cells are dropped.

list.description: A bulleted list, or numbered with "ordered": true.

items.description: An item's text, or an object without a `type`: an item with a list under it, {"text": "Build", "items": ["lint", "test"]}, numbered with "ordered": true.

code.description: Preformatted text, such as a log or a command's output, in a fixed-width font, with a button that copies it. Long lines scroll sideways.

note.description: A callout in a colour: a named colour (green, yellow, red, blue or gray, as for cards) or #rrggbb. Default gray.

quote.description: Quoted text, such as from a message or a log.

link.description: A link on a line of its own, that opens in your browser. Only http(s) urls.

image.description: A picture, as a base64 data: url of a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP or SVG image, with `alt` saying what it shows. Reports can't fetch anything, so it can't be a link.

details.description: Blocks hidden under `summary` until it's clicked, such as a long log.

not.description: a run can't be in details: it goes at the top level of a report

rule.description: A line across the report, between parts of it.

run.description: A command with a button that runs it, in a colour for how its last run went, when it started, its output (stdout and stderr) as it comes, and a button that stops it (SIGTERM to it and whatever it started). The command runs with `bash -lc` in your home directory, with nothing on its stdin; only if commands are allowed, as for cards, and otherwise the button's disabled. ledge keeps each event's last run of a command until it stops, so the report shows it when opened again; running it again replaces it. Only at the top level of a report, not in details.

title.description: The button's title; default "Run", or the theme's run icon alone.

kind.description: The kind of card, and so which other properties it takes (default: basic, a title and a description).

id.description: Send an existing id to replace that event, from the same source: an id belongs to the source that sent it. Without one, a new id is generated and returned. Give a fixed one (e.g. "aws-auth") so re-sending updates the card instead of adding another.

description.description: A line or two under the title.

url.description: Clicking the card runs `open <url>`, so it opens in whatever app handles it (https: in your browser, vscode: in VS Code). Must start with a scheme.

report.description: The details, shown in a report window when the card is clicked: a list of blocks, drawn top to bottom in the bar's theme. To change a report, send the event again with the same id.

command.description: A bash command to run when the card is clicked, e.g. a login that re-sends this event. Runs with `bash -lc` in your home directory; its output is appended to commands.log in the state directory. Refused unless ledge's config has "commands": true.

priority.description: Sorts the card, and colours it if it has no `color`.

color.description: The card's colour, until the first step of its `schedule`.

schedule.description: Colour changes. The card shows the colour of the latest step whose time has passed.

source.description: Who sent it (default: manual). A section ({source, items}) replaces all of a source's events.

not.description: only one of `url`, `report` and `command` can be set: clicking the card does one thing

then.description: A timer: counts down to `end`, filling from `start` if it has one, or counts up from `start` alone.
How far along something is, such as a deploy.

label.description: Shown instead of the percent, such as "3/5".

then.description: A number, how it's moved, and a sparkline of its history.

value.description: The number, as shown, such as "2.3%".

change_color.description: The change's colour; you say whether up is good.

history.description: Recent values, oldest first, drawn behind the card.

then.description: How a set of checks went, such as a CI run's jobs.
A message, such as a chat or an email: the title is its subject or channel, the description its start.

avatar.description: A picture of the sender, as a base64 data: URL of an image; without one, their initials show.
